findings.text: the freshness assertion passes with the renewal removed, because the child that publishes writes its own pid into the beat and the reader shares that process table, so past the shortened 1.0s stale window host_is_live falls through to _holder_is_running_here at reckon/crew/host_heartbeat.py:194 and answers True for the still-running child; the off-host reader the fix is for is exactly the one that cannot see that pid, so the case never crosses the boundary it claims.

test_the_supervisor_publishes_the_beat_it_keeps_fresh asserts only that a beat exists immediately after _supervisor_command returns, inside the default 90s stale window, so it guards publication but cannot detect a supervisor that publishes once and never renews; the name claims a freshness the assertion does not measure.

a publish landing after an ended renewal breaks out of its loop at :158 but before its finally at :160 removes the key sees the key still registered, returns without starting a renewer, and then the stale key is dropped, so the suppression this commit repairs is narrowed to a race window rather than removed.

process_runs_here repeats the recorded-start-time comparison that reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:424 record_process_alive already owns and describes as the one place the pid lookup lives, so the two can still disagree; process_runs_here adds a pid-namespace test that process_liveness omits, which is the divergence in the making.
